claims.statement: Every Slack/Linear/GitHub webhook route verifies the platform signature on the raw request body before parsing, and returns HTTP 401 on a missing or invalid signature.

Signature verification is fail-closed on a missing signing secret: verify_slack_signature, verify_github_signature, and verify_linear_signature reject the webhook when their secret is unconfigured rather than accepting unauthenticated traffic.
verify_slack_signature additionally rejects requests whose X-Slack-Request-Timestamp is more than five minutes old (max_age_seconds=300), defeating replay of a previously valid signed request.

Webhook routes do the real work in a FastAPI BackgroundTask and immediately return a fast accepted response, so signature-verify plus filtering happens inline while thread resolution and dispatch happen asynchronously.

Thread ids are deterministically derived from external identifiers so webhooks, the dashboard, and the reviewer re-derive the same id and route a follow-up to the existing thread; the formulas are a persisted routing contract and changing one orphans live threads.

The GitHub PR thread id for a branch Open SWE created is recovered by extracting the embedded UUID from the branch name via thread_id_from_branch, and otherwise falls back to pr_comment_thread_id keyed by owner/repo/PR number.

resolve_slack_thread_id resolves a Slack location to an agent thread by preferring a stored explicit mapping, else searching thread metadata for the Slack location, else deriving slack_thread_id; more than one matching thread raises SlackThreadMappingError instead of guessing.

Open SWE refuses to operate in externally shared Slack (Slack Connect) channels: slack_channel_allows_operations permits only DMs or channels Slack confirms are not externally shared, and an app_mention in an external channel receives a one-time refusal reply and is dropped.

Outside code channels a Slack message is dispatched only if it is an app_mention, a DM, a reply to a ready plan, or an untagged two-party reply where the sender and Open SWE are the only live participants; bot-authored events, the bot's own messages, and duplicate deliveries are dropped.
Slack event delivery is deduplicated with claim_slack_event, which gates the background dispatch so only the first delivery of an event id creates a run.

GitHub and Linear webhooks acknowledge the human instantly with a 👀 reaction on the triggering comment: react_to_github_comment posts the GitHub eyes reaction (GraphQL EYES for PR-review bodies) and react_to_linear_comment posts 👀 on the Linear comment.

A Slack run is blocked unless the triggering user has a valid GitHub token (except in bot-token-only mode) because Open SWE opens PRs as the triggering user; the user is prompted to link their account instead of a run being dispatched.

Whether a Slack follow-up interrupts the active run is decided by _interrupts_active_run/_is_explicit_slack_request, and _dispatch_or_queue_slack_run dispatches with multitask_strategy='interrupt' for an explicit tag and 'enqueue' otherwise.

The Linear route fires only on Comment create events that mention @open-swe and are not bot- or Open-SWE-authored, and resolves the repository in priority order: explicit owner/repo in the comment, then the commenter's dashboard default_repo, then a team/project mapping, then the team default, rejecting repos outside the allowlist.

process_linear_issue derives the thread id from the issue id via linear_issue_thread_id, resolves the triggering user's email from the comment author/creator/assignee, builds a Linear-issue system introduction plus per-author person introductions and comments, dispatches, and posts a trace comment linking the Open SWE thread.

The GitHub route multiplexes issue, comment, PR, review, push, and CI events; it requires an @open-swe mention on issue/comment events, enforces the repo allowlist and a public-repo org gate, and routes replies to Open SWE review findings to the reviewer graph separately.

process_github_pr_comment resolves the triggering user's GitHub token via their email mapping (refreshing once on a 401), gathers all comments since the last @open-swe tag, builds per-author person introductions plus one human input-message per comment, and dispatches through _trigger_or_queue_run.

Reviewer runs (auto first-review, push re-review, and finding replies) dispatch on the reviewer_thread_id namespace with assistant_id='reviewer', distinct from the agent thread and graph used for coding runs.

Content is serialized into a strict input-message envelope: each authored message becomes an <input-message> with sender/surface/kind attributes wrapping an XML-escaped <content> body, and human_input/system_input enforce that kind matches the message role.

Senders, channels, and systems are introduced once as <dynamic-context> blocks stamped with a SHA-256 hash so identities are not re-introduced every turn, and untrusted fields such as a channel topic/purpose are marked trust="untrusted".

When a caller passes plain content rather than a prebuilt RunInput, dispatch_agent_run synthesizes sender/channel/system identities from the configurable dict via _dispatch_input, mapping a Slack/GitHub/Linear sender to a namespaced sender_id and falling back to a system: actor when no human sender is present.

dispatch_agent_run routes every trigger through create_durable_run, which defaults to multitask_strategy='interrupt' so a follow-up halts the active run and resumes the agent with full history plus the new message, while background follow-ups can opt into 'enqueue'.
Durable runs use durability='sync', checkpointing before each step so a crash or container recycle resumes from the last checkpoint instead of losing all work.

A run-completion webhook is attached only when RUN_COMPLETE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set and the URL is absolute (not relative/loopback), degrading to no webhook otherwise to avoid the platform rejecting every runs.create; the secret is appended as ?token= and the receiving /webhooks/run-complete route is fail-closed on that token.

Runs are created with stream_resumable=True so a client attaching later can replay the event stream; without it the v2 protocol cannot synthesize the lifecycle running event that drives the web UI loading state for a run the UI did not start.

Dispatched runs are given the Protocol v2 stream shape — the V2_RUN_STREAM_MODES set, stream_subgraphs=True, and the EVENT_STREAMING_V2_CONFIG_KEY marker injected by prepare_run_config — so the dashboard receives tools/lifecycle channels and nested subagent namespaces for webhook-triggered runs; without the marker a run streams values only.
